drug_class: ACE Inhibitor combined with Calcium Channel Blocker
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines that work together to help lower your blood pressure and reduce the strain on your heart. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps prevent heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems.
how_it_works: Trandolapril is an ACE inhibitor — it relaxes your blood vessels by blocking a chemical in your body that causes them to tighten up. Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker — it slows down your heart rate and helps your blood vessels relax by blocking calcium from entering heart and blood vessel cells. Together, they make it easier for your heart to pump blood through your body.
common_side_effects: Constipation (very common with verapamil), dizziness or lightheadedness, headache, dry cough, feeling tired or weak, slow heartbeat, and swelling in the legs or ankles. Some people may also notice flushing or a feeling of warmth.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm the baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, heart rhythm issues, or if you are already taking other blood pressure medicines. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor approves. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet taken once a day with food. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how your blood pressure responds. Always take it at the same time each day, and never crush or chew the tablet — swallow it whole.
